requirements.text: The system shall function as an add-on module to the Sun Grid Engine (SGE) cluster management system.
The system shall support the scheduling of sequential and embarrassingly parallel batch jobs on a homogeneous Linux cluster.
The system shall implement a bid-based proportional resource-sharing model to allocate CPU time based on user-defined budget and deadline constraints.
The system shall use the stride-scheduling algorithm to enforce resource allocations proportional to job priority.
The system shall allow users to submit jobs with parameters including executable location, input data, system type, maximum execution time, budget, and deadline.
The system shall provide an interface for users to view job status, cancel jobs, and check credit balances.
The system shall provide an administrative interface to monitor node status, cluster load, usage history, and manage job execution (cancel, suspend, resume).
The system shall dynamically reallocate resources based on user-defined priorities and emergency status.
The maximum response time for job submission shall be 1 minute.
The system shall ensure that all jobs are completed within a 10% error allowance of the estimated deadline, assuming accurate input statistics.
The system shall ensure that the maximum cost charged to a user does not exceed the budget submitted by the user.
The system shall have a maximum bug rate of 1 bug per 1000 lines of code (KLOC).
The system shall recover from a system outage within 5 minutes, limited by the Linux operating system boot time.
The system shall ensure privacy of user job status and restrict administrative actions to authorized personnel.
The system shall provide command-line interfaces for users and administrators, with future support for a GUI.
The system shall be developed in standard C and follow the Hungarian Naming Convention.
The system shall be released under the GNU General Purpose License (GPL).
